sanskrit: vṛddhāv ūcatuḥ kuśalaṃ no gṛhe vipra bhṛtyavarge ca sarvaśaḥ kaccit tvam apy avighnena saṃprāpto bhagavann iha
english: The two elders said: All is well in our home, O brahmin, and among our servants in every respect. And have you yourself arrived here without obstacle, O venerable one?

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca bāḍham ity eva tau vipraḥ pratyuvāca mudānvitaḥ dharmavyādhas tu taṃ vipram arthavad vākyam abravīt
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: The brahmin replied to them both with the word "Indeed," filled with joy. And Dharma-the-hunter then spoke a meaningful word to that brahmin.

sanskrit: pitā mātā ca bhagavann etau me daivataṃ param yad daivatebhyaḥ kartavyaṃ tad etābhyāṃ karomy aham
english: "Father and mother, O venerable one, are my highest deity. Whatever is to be done for the gods — that I do for these two."

sanskrit: trayastriṃśad yathā devāḥ sarve śakrapurogamāḥ saṃpūjyāḥ sarvalokasya tathā vṛddhāv imau mama
english: "Just as the thirty-three gods, all headed by Indra, are to be worshipped by all the worlds, so are these two elders to me."

sanskrit: upahārān āharanto devatānāṃ yathā dvijāḥ kurvate tadvad etābhyāṃ karomy aham atandritaḥ
english: "Just as brahmins bring offerings and perform rites for the gods, so I serve these two, tirelessly."

sanskrit: etau me paramaṃ brahman pitā mātā ca daivatam etau puṣpaiḥ phalai ratnais toṣayāmi sadā dvija
english: "These two — my father and my mother — are my supreme deity, O brahmin. I always please them with flowers, fruits, and jewels, O twice-born."

sanskrit: etāv evāgnayo mahyaṃ yān vadanti manīṣiṇaḥ yajñā vedāś ca catvāraḥ sarvam etau mama dvija
english: "These two indeed are the sacred fires for me that the wise speak of; they are the sacrifices, the four Vedas — they are everything to me, O twice-born."

sanskrit: etadarthaṃ mama prāṇā bhāryā putrāḥ suhṛjjanāḥ saputradāraḥ śuśrūṣāṃ nityam eva karomy aham
english: "For their sake are my very life-breaths, my wife, my sons, my dear ones. Together with sons and wife I render them service constantly."

sanskrit: svayaṃ ca snāpayāmy etau tathā pādau pradhāvaye āhāraṃ saṃprayacchāmi svayaṃ ca dvijasattama
english: "I myself bathe them; I wash their feet as well; I personally give them their food, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: anukūlāḥ kathā vacmi vipriyaṃ parivarjayan adharmeṇāpi saṃyuktaṃ priyam ābhyāṃ karomy aham
english: "I speak pleasing words, avoiding whatever is disagreeable. Even what may be joined with unrighteousness, if it pleases them, I do for these two."

sanskrit: dharmam eva guruṃ jñātvā karomi dvijasattama atandritaḥ sadā vipra śuśrūṣāṃ vai karomy aham
english: "Knowing dharma itself as my guru, I act, O best of twice-born. I always serve them tirelessly, O brahmin — this indeed is my service."

sanskrit: pañcaiva guravo brahman puruṣasya bubhūṣataḥ pitā mātāgnir ātmā ca guruś ca dvijasattama
english: "There are exactly five gurus for a person who wishes to prosper, O brahmin: father, mother, fire, the self, and the teacher, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: eteṣu yas tu varteta samyag eva dvijottama bhaveyur agnayas tasya paricīrṇās tu nityaśaḥ gārhasthye vartamānasya dharma eṣa sanātanaḥ
english: "One who conducts himself rightly toward these, O best of twice-born, shall have his sacred fires perpetually tended. This is the eternal dharma for one living the householder's life."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca gurū nivedya viprāya tau mātāpitarāv ubhau punar eva sa dharmātmā vyādho brāhmaṇam abravīt
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having presented both his parents — his two gurus — to the brahmin, that righteous-souled hunter again spoke to the brahmin.

sanskrit: pravṛttacakṣur jāto 'smi saṃpaśya tapaso balam yadartham ukto 'si tayā gacchasva mithilām iti
english: "I have gained insight; behold the power of austerity. This is the very reason she told you: 'Go to Mithilā.'"

sanskrit: patiśuśrūṣaparayā dāntayā satyaśīlayā mithilāyāṃ vasan vyādhaḥ sa te dharmān pravakṣyati
english: "By the devoted, self-restrained, truthful woman whose highest calling is service to her husband, it was said: 'The hunter dwelling in Mithilā will expound dharma to you.'"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca pativratāyāḥ satyāyāḥ śīlāḍhyāyā yatavrata saṃsmṛtya vākyaṃ dharmajña guṇavān asi me mataḥ
english: The brahmin said: "Calling to mind the word of that faithful wife, truthful and abounding in noble character, O man of discipline — you are, O knower of dharma, one endowed with virtue in my judgment."

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca yat tadā tvaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha tayokto māṃ prati prabho dṛṣṭam etat tayā samyag ekapatnyā na saṃśayaḥ
english: The hunter said: "What she told you then regarding me, O best of twice-born, O lord — that has been truly seen by her, that woman of single husband. There is no doubt."

sanskrit: tvadanugrahabuddhyā tu vipraitad darśitaṃ mayā vākyaṃ ca śṛṇu me tāta yat te vakṣye hitaṃ dvija
english: "With the intention of doing you a favor, O brahmin, I have shown you this. And now hear my word, dear one — what I shall speak for your benefit, O twice-born."

sanskrit: tvayā vinikṛtā mātā pitā ca dvijasattama anisṛṣṭo 'si niṣkrānto gṛhāt tābhyām anindita vedoccāraṇakāryārtham ayuktaṃ tat tvayā kṛtam
english: "Your mother and father have been wronged by you, O best of twice-born. Without their leave you departed from the house, O blameless one — for the purpose of Veda recitation. That was not fitting of you."

sanskrit: tava śokena vṛddhau tāv andhau jātau tapasvinau tau prasādayituṃ gaccha mā tvā dharmo 'tyagān mahān
english: "Those two aged and ascetic ones have gone blind from grief over you. Go and appease them — let not great dharma abandon you."

sanskrit: tapasvī tvaṃ mahātmā ca dharme ca nirataḥ sadā sarvam etad apārthaṃ te kṣipraṃ tau saṃprasādaya
english: "You are an ascetic, a great soul, ever intent upon dharma — yet all of that is fruitless for you. Go quickly and propitiate those two."

sanskrit: śraddadhasva mama brahman nānyathā kartum arhasi gamyatām adya viprarṣe śreyas te kathayāmy aham
english: "Have faith in my words, O brahmin — you must not do otherwise. Depart this very day, O sage among brahmins. I am telling you what is good for you."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca yad etad uktaṃ bhavatā sarvaṃ satyam asaṃśayam prīto 'smi tava dharmajña sādhvācāra guṇānvita
english: The brahmin said: "All that you have said is true without doubt. I am pleased with you, O knower of dharma, O man of good conduct, endowed with virtue."

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca daivatapratimo hi tvaṃ yas tvaṃ dharmam anuvrataḥ purāṇaṃ śāśvataṃ divyaṃ duṣprāpam akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: The hunter said: "You are indeed equal to a deity, you who are devoted to dharma — that ancient, eternal, divine dharma that is unattainable by those who have not refined their souls."

sanskrit: atandritaḥ kuru kṣipraṃ mātāpitror hi pūjanam ataḥ param ahaṃ dharmaṃ nānyaṃ paśyāmi kaṃ cana
english: "Tirelessly and quickly perform the worship of your mother and father. Beyond this, I see no other dharma whatsoever."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca ihāham āgato diṣṭyā diṣṭyā me saṃgataṃ tvayā īdṛśā durlabhā loke narā dharmapradarśakāḥ
english: The brahmin said: "By good fortune I came here; by good fortune I met with you. Such men as reveal dharma are rare in this world."

sanskrit: eko narasahasreṣu dharmavid vidyate na vā prīto 'smi tava satyena bhadraṃ te puruṣottama
english: "Scarcely one among a thousand men, or perhaps none, truly knows dharma. I am satisfied by your truthfulness. May good come to you, O best of men."

sanskrit: patamāno hi narake bhavatāsmi samuddhṛtaḥ bhavitavyam athaivaṃ ca yad dṛṣṭo 'si mayānagha
english: "As I was falling into hell, I have been rescued by you. It was destined to be thus — that I would see you, O sinless one."

sanskrit: rājā yayātir dauhitraiḥ patitas tārito yathā sadbhiḥ puruṣaśārdūla tathāhaṃ bhavatā tv iha
english: "Just as King Yayāti, fallen, was saved by his grandsons — good men — O tiger among men, so have I been saved here by you."

sanskrit: mātāpitṛbhyāṃ śuśrūṣāṃ kariṣye vacanāt tava nākṛtātmā vedayati dharmādharmaviniścayam
english: "I shall render service to my mother and father at your word. One who has not disciplined himself does not discern the determination of dharma and adharma."

sanskrit: durjñeyaḥ śāśvato dharmaḥ śūdrayonau hi vartatā na tvāṃ śūdram ahaṃ manye bhavitavyaṃ hi kāraṇam yena karmavipākena prāpteyaṃ śūdratā tvayā
english: "Eternal dharma is hard to know, yet here it dwells in a shudra birth. I do not regard you as a shudra — there must be a cause, some ripening of past karma, by which this shudra state has come to you."

sanskrit: etad icchāmi vijñātuṃ tattvena hi mahāmate kāmayā brūhi me tathyaṃ sarvaṃ tvaṃ prayatātmavān
english: "This I wish to understand truly, O great mind. Please tell me everything truthfully — you who are of disciplined soul."

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca anatikramaṇīyā hi brāhmaṇā vai dvijottama śṛṇu sarvam idaṃ vṛttaṃ pūrvadehe mamānagha
english: The hunter said: "Brahmins are not to be transgressed, O best of twice-born. Hear all that transpired in my former birth, O sinless one."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi brāhmaṇaḥ pūrvam āsaṃ dvijavarātmaja vedādhyāyī sukuśalo vedāṅgānāṃ ca pāragaḥ ātmadoṣakṛtair brahmann avasthāṃ prāptavān imām
english: "I was indeed a brahmin formerly, O son of the best twice-born — a student of the Vedas, well skilled, a master of the Vedic auxiliaries. By my own faults I have come to this condition, O brahmin."

sanskrit: kaś cid rājā mama sakhā dhanurvedaparāyaṇaḥ saṃsargād dhanuṣi śreṣṭhas tato 'ham abhavaṃ dvija
english: "A certain king was my friend, devoted to the science of archery. Through association with him I became excellent in the bow, O twice-born."

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu mṛgayāṃ nirgato nṛpaḥ sahito yodhamukhyaiś ca mantribhiś ca susaṃvṛtaḥ tato 'bhyahan mṛgāṃs tatra subahūn āśramaṃ prati
english: "At that very time the king went out hunting, accompanied by his chief warriors and ministers, well attended. And there he slew very many deer near an ashrama."

sanskrit: atha kṣiptaḥ śaro ghoro mayāpi dvijasattama tāḍitaś ca munis tena śareṇānataparvaṇā
english: "Then I too released a terrible arrow, O best of twice-born, and a sage was struck by that arrow with its joints bent back."

sanskrit: bhūmau nipatito brahmann uvāca pratinādayan nāparādhyāmy ahaṃ kiṃ cit kena pāpam idaṃ kṛtam
english: "Fallen to the ground, O brahmin, he cried out resonantly: 'I have done no wrong — by whom has this evil been done?'"

sanskrit: manvānas taṃ mṛgaṃ cāhaṃ saṃprāptaḥ sahasā munim apaśyaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ viddhaṃ śareṇānataparvaṇā tam ugratapasaṃ vipraṃ niṣṭanantaṃ mahītale
english: "Thinking it a deer, I had hastily approached and suddenly saw that sage — the seer pierced by the arrow with bent joints, that brahmin of fierce austerity, groaning upon the earth."

sanskrit: akāryakaraṇāc cāpi bhṛśaṃ me vyathitaṃ manaḥ ajānatā kṛtam idaṃ mayety atha tam abruvam kṣantum arhasi me brahmann iti cokto mayā muniḥ
english: "My mind was deeply distressed at having done this unlawful act. 'This was done by me unknowingly,' I thought, and I said to him: 'You must forgive me, O brahmin.' Thus spoken to by me, the sage —"

sanskrit: tataḥ pratyabravīd vākyam ṛṣir māṃ krodhamūrchitaḥ vyādhas tvaṃ bhavitā krūra śūdrayonāv iti dvija
english: "— then spoke back a word to me, overcome with rage: 'You shall be a cruel hunter, born in a shudra womb,' O twice-born."

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca evaṃ śapto 'ham ṛṣiṇā tadā dvijavarottama abhiprasādayam ṛṣiṃ girā vākyaviśāradam
english: The hunter said: "Thus cursed by the sage at that time, O best among the twice-born, I sought to appease the sage with speech, skilled in words."

sanskrit: ajānatā mayākāryam idam adya kṛtaṃ mune kṣantum arhasi tat sarvaṃ prasīda bhagavann iti
english: "'This unlawful act has been done by me today unknowingly, O sage. You must forgive all of it. Be gracious, O venerable one.'"

sanskrit: ṛṣir uvāca nānyathā bhavitā śāpa evam etad asaṃśayam ānṛśaṃsyād ahaṃ kiṃ cit kartānugraham adya te
english: The sage said: "The curse cannot be otherwise — so it shall be, without doubt. Out of compassion I will bestow some grace upon you today."

sanskrit: śūdrayonau vartamāno dharmajño bhavitā hy asi mātāpitroś ca śuśrūṣāṃ kariṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Though dwelling in a shudra birth, you shall be a knower of dharma, and you shall render service to your mother and father — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: tayā śuśrūṣayā siddhiṃ mahatīṃ samavāpsyasi jātismaraś ca bhavitā svargaṃ caiva gamiṣyasi śāpakṣayānte nirvṛtte bhavitāsi punar dvijaḥ
english: "Through that service you shall attain great perfection. You shall remember your former birth, and you shall go to heaven as well. When the curse is exhausted and spent, you shall become a twice-born again."

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca evaṃ śaptaḥ purā tena ṛṣiṇāsmy ugratejasā prasādaś ca kṛtas tena mamaivaṃ dvipadāṃ vara
english: The hunter said: "Thus was I cursed of old by that sage of fierce splendor, and such grace was bestowed upon me by him, O best among bipeds."

sanskrit: śaraṃ coddhṛtavān asmi tasya vai dvijasattama āśramaṃ ca mayā nīto na ca prāṇair vyayujyata
english: "And I drew out the arrow from him, O best of twice-born, and brought him to his ashrama. And he did not lose his life-breaths."

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yathā mama purābhavat abhitaś cāpi gantavyaṃ mayā svargaṃ dvijottama
english: "All this has been told to you, as it came to pass for me long ago. And I am also to go to heaven soon, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca evam etāni puruṣā duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca prāpnuvanti mahābuddhe notkaṇṭhāṃ kartum arhasi duṣkaraṃ hi kṛtaṃ tāta jānatā jātim ātmanaḥ
english: The brahmin said: "Thus do men obtain sorrows and joys alike, O great-minded one. You should not be troubled. What is difficult has been accomplished — remembering your own previous birth, dear friend."

sanskrit: karmadoṣaś ca vai vidvann ātmajātikṛtena vai kaṃ cit kālaṃ mṛṣyatāṃ vai tato 'si bhavitā dvijaḥ sāṃprataṃ ca mato me 'si brāhmaṇo nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "The fault of karma produced by one's own past birth — endure it for a while, O learned one, and then you shall be a twice-born again. Even now I regard you as a brahmin; of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaḥ patanīyeṣu vartamāno vikarmasu dāmbhiko duṣkṛtaprāyaḥ śūdreṇa sadṛśo bhavet
english: "A brahmin who engages in degrading acts, who is hypocritical and given largely to evil deeds, becomes equal to a shudra."

sanskrit: yas tu śūdro dame satye dharme ca satatotthitaḥ taṃ brāhmaṇam ahaṃ manye vṛttena hi bhaved dvijaḥ
english: "But a shudra who is ever intent upon self-restraint, truth, and dharma — him I regard as a brahmin. For it is by conduct that one becomes twice-born."

sanskrit: karmadoṣeṇa viṣamāṃ gatim āpnoti dāruṇām kṣīṇadoṣam ahaṃ manye cābhitas tvāṃ narottama
english: "By the fault of karma one obtains a terrible and unequal condition. I regard your fault as already exhausted on all sides, O best of men."

sanskrit: kartum arhasi notkaṇṭhāṃ tvadvidhā hy aviṣādinaḥ lokavṛttāntavṛttajñā nityaṃ dharmaparāyaṇāḥ
english: "You should not be troubled. Those like you are undiscouraged, knowers of how the world conducts itself, ever devoted to dharma."

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca prajñayā mānasaṃ duḥkhaṃ hanyāc chārīram auṣadhaiḥ etad vijñānasāmarthyaṃ na bālaiḥ samatāṃ vrajet
english: The hunter said: "Mental suffering is to be conquered by wisdom, bodily suffering by remedies. This is the power of knowledge — it should not be equated with the condition of fools."

sanskrit: aniṣṭasaṃprayogāc ca viprayogāt priyasya ca mānuṣā mānasair duḥkhair yujyante alpabuddhayaḥ
english: "From conjunction with the unwanted and from separation from what is dear, men of little understanding are yoked to mental sorrows."

sanskrit: guṇair bhūtāni yujyante viyujyante tathaiva ca sarvāṇi naitad ekasya śokasthānaṃ hi vidyate
english: "Beings are joined together by the qualities of nature and separated by them as well — all of them. This is not a cause for grief for any single person alone."

sanskrit: aniṣṭenānvitaṃ paśyaṃs tathā kṣipraṃ virajyate tataś ca pratikurvanti yadi paśyanty upakramam śocato na bhavet kiṃ cit kevalaṃ paritapyate
english: "Seeing one connected with the unwanted, a person quickly turns away. And then they counteract it if they see a remedy. For one who laments, nothing is gained — he merely burns himself."

sanskrit: parityajanti ye duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ vāpy ubhayaṃ narāḥ ta eva sukham edhante jñānatṛptā manīṣiṇaḥ
english: "Those men who abandon both sorrow and joy alike — they indeed prosper in happiness, those wise ones satisfied by knowledge."

sanskrit: asaṃtoṣaparā mūḍhāḥ saṃtoṣaṃ yānti paṇḍitāḥ asaṃtoṣasya nāsty antas tuṣṭis tu paramaṃ sukham na śocanti gatādhvānaḥ paśyantaḥ paramāṃ gatim
english: "The deluded are devoted to discontent; the wise attain contentment. There is no end to discontent, but contentment is the highest happiness. Those who have traveled the path and see the highest goal do not grieve."

sanskrit: na viṣāde manaḥ kāryaṃ viṣādo viṣam uttamam mārayaty akṛtaprajñaṃ bālaṃ kruddha ivoragaḥ
english: "One must not set the mind on dejection. Dejection is a supreme poison — it kills the unwise child, like an enraged serpent."

sanskrit: yaṃ viṣādo 'bhibhavati viṣame samupasthite tejasā tasya hīnasya puruṣārtho na vidyate
english: "One whom dejection overpowers when adversity presents itself — that man, diminished in his luster, has no human purpose left."

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ kriyamāṇasya karmaṇo dṛśyate phalam na hi nirvedam āgamya kiṃ cit prāpnoti śobhanam
english: "The fruit of action necessarily performed is seen. For by coming to despondency one obtains nothing excellent."

sanskrit: athāpy upāyaṃ paśyeta duḥkhasya parimokṣaṇe aśocann ārabhetaiva yuktaś cāvyasanī bhavet
english: "But if one sees a means for the removal of suffering, one should begin without lamenting, being disciplined and free from addiction."

sanskrit: bhūteṣv abhāvaṃ saṃcintya ye tu buddheḥ paraṃ gatāḥ na śocanti kṛtaprajñāḥ paśyantaḥ paramāṃ gatim
english: "Those who have gone beyond the intellect, contemplating the transience of beings, do not grieve — those of mature wisdom who see the highest goal."

sanskrit: na śocāmi ca vai vidvan kālākāṅkṣī sthito 'smy aham etair nidarśanair brahman nāvasīdāmi sattama
english: "I do not grieve, O learned one; I stand awaiting my time. By these examples, O brahmin, I do not sink, O excellent one."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca kṛtaprajño 'si medhāvī buddhiś ca vipulā tava nāhaṃ bhavantaṃ śocāmi jñānatṛpto 'si dharmavit
english: The brahmin said: "You are of mature wisdom, of great intelligence, and your understanding is vast. I do not grieve for you — you are satisfied by knowledge, O knower of dharma."

sanskrit: āpṛcche tvāṃ svasti te 'stu dharmas tvā parirakṣatu apramādas tu kartavyo dharme dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: "I take my leave of you. May it be well with you. May dharma protect you. Vigilance must be maintained in dharma, O best among those who uphold it."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca bāḍham ity eva taṃ vyādhaḥ kṛtāñjalir uvāca ha pradakṣiṇam atho kṛtvā prasthito dvijasattamaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: "Indeed so," said the hunter to him, his hands folded in reverence. And then, having performed the circumambulation, that best of twice-born departed.

sanskrit: sa tu gatvā dvijaḥ sarvāṃ śuśrūṣāṃ kṛtavāṃs tadā mātāpitṛbhyāṃ vṛddhābhyāṃ yathānyāyaṃ susaṃśitaḥ
english: And that brahmin, having gone, rendered full service then to his two aged parents — mother and father — properly and with great discipline.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ nikhilena yudhiṣṭhira pṛṣṭavān asi yaṃ tāta dharmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: "All this has been told to you completely, O Yudhiṣṭhira. The dharma you asked about, dear one, O best among those who uphold dharma."

sanskrit: pativratāyā māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇasya ca sattama mātāpitroś ca śuśrūṣā vyādhe dharmaś ca kīrtitaḥ
english: "The greatness of the devoted wife, and of the brahmin, O excellent one; the service of mother and father; and the dharma in the hunter — all have been proclaimed."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca atyadbhutam idaṃ brahman dharmākhyānam anuttamam sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha kathitaṃ dvijasattama
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "This account of dharma is supremely wonderful and unsurpassed, O brahmin — told by you, O best among all who uphold dharma, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: sukhaśravyatayā vidvan muhūrtam iva me gatam na hi tṛpto 'smi bhagavañ śṛṇvāno dharmam uttamam
english: "By its sweetness of hearing, O learned one, it passed for me as but a moment. I am not yet satisfied, O venerable one, hearing this highest dharma."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvemāṃ dharmasaṃyuktāṃ dharmarājaḥ kathāṃ śubhām punaḥ papraccha tam ṛṣiṃ mārkaṇḍeyaṃ tapasvinam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this auspicious tale joined with dharma, the King of Dharma again questioned the ascetic sage Mārkaṇḍeya.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca katham agnir vanaṃ yātaḥ kathaṃ cāpy aṅgirāḥ purā naṣṭe 'gnau havyam avahad agnir bhūtvā mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "How did Agni go to the forest? And how did Aṅgiras in former times, when fire had disappeared, carry the oblation, himself having become a great sage-fire?"

sanskrit: agnir yadā tv eka eva bahutvaṃ cāsya karmasu dṛśyate bhagavan sarvam etad icchāmi veditum
english: "When fire is one alone, yet multiplicity of it is seen in its functions, O venerable one — all of this I wish to know."

sanskrit: kumāraś ca yathotpanno yathā cāgneḥ suto 'bhavat yathā rudrāc ca saṃbhūto gaṅgāyāṃ kṛttikāsu ca
english: "And how was Kumāra born? How did he become the son of Agni? How was he produced from Rudra, and in the Gaṅgā, and among the Kṛttikās?"
